turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, take a seat. I'm Doctor Reilly. What has you in this morning?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks a million, doctor. I'm Nuala, his mam. He was in bits after training yesterday, so I brought him down.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I twisted my left ankle at training yesterday. It is swollen, and it is quite painful when I walk.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yesterday, at training. Tell me how it happened, in your own words.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): I planted the left foot and it rolled outwards. There was a pop. I had to stop the drill.
[SEG0006] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he could not put a pick of weight on it. Sure I nearly carried him from the car into the waiting room just now.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Mam, that isn't quite accurate. I walked in from the car on my own. It is sore, but I can bear my weight.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. So you walked in, with pain, and your mam felt you couldn't weight it at all. We'll look at that in a minute. Where is the swelling?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): On the outside of the left ankle. It feels like I've a balloon tied on under the skin.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): A balloon, so swelling on the outer side. Did that come up straight away?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Within the hour, I would say. The pain is like someone has driven a nail in, just below the bone. It is there all the time, and walking makes it worse.
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He went pure white on the sideline. The place was roaring, I couldn't hear myself think, so I just got him into the car.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): I was shaken for a minute, yes. I am perfectly all right in myself now. I do think I have overdone the training this month, but that is a separate matter.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any numbness or pins and needles in the toes? Pain in the knee, or up the shin?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No numbness, and the knee and the shin are fine.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grand. Have you injured this same ankle before?

[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, last spring. They sent me for an x-ray at the hospital. They said it was borderline, they could not tell if there was a tiny chip or if it was just the angle of the picture.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Borderline, not called a definite break. Are you taking any medicines at the moment?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): I took two paracetemol last night, umm, five hundred milligrams each. I have taken nothing since, and I don't take anything regularly.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two paracetemol, five hundred each, last night only. Any allergy to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor. No allergies that I am aware of.
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's never reacted to a thing. He had penicillin as a small lad and he was grand on it.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. No known allergies, and penicillin suited him. Do you train much, or is it the odd evening?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): I train with the club four evenings a week, and we have a match most Sundays. I am in fifth year at school.
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he'll be raging if he misses Sunday. Your man the coach already texted, but that's neither here nor there.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Four evenings and a match, fifth year. Hop up on the couch, left ankle towards me. Tell me if I hit a sore bit.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Of course. It is tender just there, on the front of the outer ankle.

[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Soft swelling over the lateral malleolus, and a little bruising starting. Tender over the ligament at the front, not along the back edge of the bone. The inner side is quiet, the pulses are there, and you should feel me on the toes.
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, I can feel that.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grand. Walk four steps to the door and back, as best you can.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Certainly. It hurts, but I can do it.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): You managed four steps, limping, taking weight. Pulse while you were sitting was 72. Blood pressure on the machine is 118 over 74, and there's no fever to my hand.
[SEG0033] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His pulse is usually lower, he's fit. Last time at the club they had it about fifty. Is 72 a worry?

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Seventy-two is a normal pulse in the chair, don't mind the fifty from the club. The Ottawa ankle rules, I'll say them plainly. We x-ray if there's bony tenderness at the back of either malleolus, or if you cannot take four steps both at the injury and here. I nearly said the midfoot bones as well, but for this twist it's the malleoli I'm using, and you're not tender on the bone.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): So you do not think it is broken?

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a lateral ligament sprain of the left ankle, not a fracture. That is provisional. I can't swear to the bone without a film, but on those rules you don't need an x-ray today.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): I understand. What ought I to do with it?

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Rest it, and keep it up higher than your heart when you sit. Ice through a cloth, about twenty minutes, a few times a day, and no training or match until I say. I'll prescribe ibuprofen, four hundred milligrams by mouth, three times a day with food, for five days, for the pain and the swelling.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you. I will take it with food.

[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse will see you Thursday morning, half nine, to check the swelling and fit a lace-up brace. That's booked, so come with the ankle bare, and there's no fasting. I'll see you myself in two weeks.
[SEG0041] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if it's worse before that, doctor?

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the pain gets worse, or he cannot bear weight, we do an x-ray. If that x-ray is borderline, or the ankle has not settled when I see you, we do an ultrasound. Otherwise we leave the pictures alone, and reception will hand you both cards on the way out.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): That is very clear. Thank you, doctor. I will rest it, and I will be here on Thursday and again in two weeks.

spec.situation: Young player who twisted the ankle yesterday; swelling, can bear weight with pain; doctor applies Ottawa rules aloud, no X-ray unless it worsens; rest and elevation advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
